newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IBIS DAX ends slightly up, well off highs.
newsitem.headline: German IBIS DAX ends slightly up, well off highs.

text.p: Germany's blue-chip DAX index registered its second closing high in a row on Tuesday, but shares came off highs in electronic trade later on to end the day only slightly ahead.

Sharp falls in chemical shares dragged the market lower in the afternoon, but dealers said the bullish trend was intact and there was no sign of a consolidation to slow its advance and the market had the next key threshold of 3,500 points still in its sights.

The DAX index of 30 German leading shares ended the day at 3,460.59 points, up 0.71 percent, while the IBIS DAX, which tracks electronic trade, ended at 3,430.95 points, up 4.18 points or 0.12 percent.
"There has been a pause in the dollar, but it is still off lows and basically it's liquidity that is taking this market up," a trader said.
Chemical shares were the main focus of attention in afternoon IBIS trade.
Hoechst AG announced lower than expected dividend and earnings figures for 1996, which saw the share end the day down 4.99 percent at 75.20 marks.

Market expectations were disappointed when the group proposed a dividend of 1.40 marks for 1996, compared to a forecast of 1.60 marks. Pre-tax profits rose 29 percent to 5.28 billion marks, against forecasts of a 50 percent rise.
"Hoechst was disappointing, but with a stock like that and with the market the way it is at the moment you have got a lot of room for profit-taking," a trader said.

The fall affected other large chemical companies also, with Bayer ending down 2.92 percent at 74.85 marks and BASF down 1.79 percent at 64.77 marks. Bayer and BASF are also reporting 1996 results this week and next week.

There was also keen interest in the banking sector. Mortgage lender DePfa Bank ended the day ahead at 87 marks, up 8.07 percent. Earlier it said that it believed that Swiss giant UBS had amassed a nine-percent stake in it.
UBS denied the claim saying it held less than one percent in DePfa and added that it had no intention of taking it over.
Deutsche Bank hit an all-time high over the course of the day to hit 95.70 marks, but came off these highs to end at 94.45 marks, up 1.35 marks.
Commerzbank ended up 1.05 marks at 45.95 marks, while Dresdner ended up 60 pfennigs at 57.35 marks.
Deutsche Telekom was another share to hit an all-time high of 35.22 marks in the heady trading climate of Tuesday afternoon.
Dealers said the share was boosted after it penetrated an important technical level. By the end of electronic trade the share was up 87 pfennigs at 34.83 marks.
The share was also lifted when its chairman Ron Sommer said he expected profits at Telekom to double this year.
Adidas AG shares advanced strongly over the day, but ended down 6.20 marks, or 3.98 percent, at 162.30 marks amid profit-taking, analysts said.
